title: ReVeil: Unconstrained Concealed Backdoor Attack on Deep Neural Networks using Machine Unlearning
problem: Existing concealed backdoor attacks on DNNs require white-box/black-box model access or auxiliary data; this work targets data collection phase without model access.
motivation: Advanced defenses detect anomalous inferences, but concealed backdoors with low pre-deployment ASR can evade detection and restore high ASR post-deployment.
method: ReVeil embeds backdoors during data collection phase of training without requiring model or auxiliary data access. It maintains low pre-deployment attack success rate through data poisoning, then restores high ASR via machine unlearning.
key_novelty: Unconstrained concealed backdoor requiring no model access or auxiliary data by targeting the data collection pipeline itself.
contributions: Achieves low pre-deployment ASR across four datasets and four trigger patterns
Successfully evades three popular backdoor detection methods
Restores high ASR post-deployment through machine unlearning
Requires only data collection phase access, not model access

metrics.accuracy: maintains low pre-deployment ASR, high post-deployment ASR

limitations: Not discussed; focus is on attack feasibility rather than defense.
primary_theme: Concealed backdoor attack via data poisoning and machine unlearning
